newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse rebounds in low volume.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse rebounds in low volume.

text.p: The Brussels bourse rose strongly on Monday morning, shrugging of Friday's weak Wall Street close, but traders said that volume was low and the rise more technical than fundamental.
"It is higher this morning, but there is no particular reason," one trader said. "We were down sharply on Friday and this is mainly a correction. But volume is very low."
The Bel-20 share index, which lost 21.27 points on Friday, was up 0.89 percent or 19.59 points at 2,221.81 by 0945 GMT, with 400 million francs of Belgian shares traded.
The opening was delayed for an hour by technical problems.
Analysts noted that the index appeared to be in the process of forming a "W" feature on the charts, which could presage a trend reversal if it becomes fully formed.

Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere featured on the rising market, up 1.9 percent to 2,965 francs in thin volume of just 5,600 shares. Traders said the rise was due to the stronger dollar and a reaction to Friday's weak close.
Utility Electrabel was up 0.6 percent at 8,090 francs after news late on Friday that the European Commission had dropped its opposition to proposed long-term local authority supply contracts.
Generale Bank said it rated the share a 'buy'.
Spot market textiles stock Sioen Industries, which said 1996 net profit was up 51 percent after Friday's close, was indicated five percent up from its 2,390 francs close.
